title: Dot diagrams, histograms and stem-and-leaf diagrams
summary: Read distributions accurately from dot diagrams, histograms and stem-and-leaf diagrams, including unequal class widths.
objectives: Read frequencies, clusters, gaps and spread from dot diagrams.
Decode ordered values and keys in stem-and-leaf diagrams.
Interpret histogram area and frequency density when class widths differ.

blocks.text: Each dot represents one observation. Read the horizontal scale first, then count stacked dots to obtain a frequency. The layout exposes repeated values, gaps, clusters and possible outliers while preserving every observation. Range is the greatest value minus the least value.

A stem-and-leaf diagram orders exact observations while showing distribution shape. The key is essential: 4|7 may mean 47, 4.7 or another scale. For back-to-back diagrams, both leaf sets share the same stem but extend in opposite directions.

Histogram bars touch because the variable is continuous. With equal class widths, frequency comparisons can use bar heights. With unequal widths, bar area represents frequency and height represents frequency density: frequency density = frequency divided by class width.

sections.title: Interpret unequal widths

prompt.text: A class of width 5 has density 4 and a class of width 10 has density 2. Find both frequencies.

content.text: Use frequency = class width × frequency density.

sections.verification_note: Equal bar areas confirm equal frequencies even though the heights differ.

sections.title: Read a stem-and-leaf diagram

prompt.text: The row 3 | 1 4 4 8 has key 3|1=31. Find its median and range.

sections.verification_note: All four values were preserved by the display.

prompt.text: A class of width 6 has frequency density 3. Find its frequency.

feedback.text: Frequency equals class width multiplied by density: 6×3=18.

blocks.text: Read the scale, key, class boundaries and units before calculating or interpreting.
Show the statistical definition or formula, calculate carefully, then explain what the result means for the displayed data.
